---
title: "What the metrics can and cannot tell us"
subtitle: "Paper 6 in a series on UK All-Weather racing outcomes"
author: "Patrick Gillen"
date: "2026-09-11"
abstract: |
  Return on investment has been reported throughout this series, alongside the
  ranking measures, and it cannot carry the model-to-model comparison on its
  own. Section 1 shows why: of the four consecutive-model differences in
  single-bet win return, recomputed on one bet rule so they read as a
  sequence, only the first step is distinguishable from zero, the three later
  intervals running
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); d <- targets::tar_read(p6m_contrasts, store = S); d <- d[!d$excludes_zero, ]; sprintf("%.0f to %.0f", 100 * min(d$ci_hi - d$ci_lo), 100 * max(d$ci_hi - d$ci_lo)) })`
  points wide against point differences no larger than
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); d <- targets::tar_read(p6m_contrasts, store = S); d <- d[!d$excludes_zero, ]; sprintf("%.0f", 100 * max(abs(d$diff_point))) })`;
  and the same model under the same rule moves
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); d <- targets::tar_read(p6m_race_sets, store = S); sprintf("%.0f", 100 * (d$roi[1] - d$roi[2])) })`
  points between two adjacent sets of races. Section 2 keeps both of Owen's
  scoring rules, which score different outcomes — P1 the race, P2 the
  runner-rows as independent binary events — and recomputes them on disjoint
  bins instead of nested thresholds, against two benchmarks: the
  over-round-adjusted settled starting price and the overnight racecard
  forecast price. On
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); d <- targets::tar_read(p6m_p2_cover, store = S); format(d$rows_panel, big.mark = ",") })`
  runner-rows both rules give the same ordering, every model loses to the
  starting price and beats the forecast price with all twelve intervals
  excluding zero, and both rules separate the paper-5 encoder from the two
  earlier models where the return could not. Section 3 fits how much of the
  model's disagreement with the forecast price the market later accepts: the
  pooled coefficient is
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); d <- targets::tar_read(p6m_beta, store = S); sprintf("%.3f", d$estimate[d$term == "slope"]) })`
  with a standard error of
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); d <- targets::tar_read(p6m_beta, store = S); sprintf("%.3f", d$se[d$term == "slope"]) })`,
  so the market's later move goes about two thirds of the way in the encoder's
  direction — though a forecast is a published opinion rather than a traded
  price, which makes that an upper bound.
format:
  html: default
  pdf:
    toc: true
    number-sections: true
bibliography: references.bib
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(targets)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# Paper 6 reads the paper-6 store. Like papers 4 and 5 and unlike papers 1-3
# this does NOT call tar_config_set(): that writes the project-root
# `_targets.yaml`, which papers 1-3's own setup chunks also write, and
# pointing it at `_targets_p6` would send their next render at the wrong
# store. Passing `store =` per call leaves `_targets.yaml` untouched.
P6_ROOT <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj"))
P6_STORE <- file.path(P6_ROOT, "_targets_p6")

source(file.path(P6_ROOT, "papers", "06_metrics", "_helpers.R"))

# tar_load() centrally so tarchetypes::tar_quarto() picks these up as render
# dependencies — files pulled in via {{< include >}} are not auto-scanned.
tar_load(c(
  # identity and gates
  p6m_race_identity, p6m_basis_check, p6m_recompute_check,
  # section 1
  p6m_series, p6m_published, p6m_contrasts, p6m_backtests_main,
  # section 1b
  p6m_val_halves, p6m_race_sets,
  # section 2
  p6m_p2_cover, p6m_scores, p6m_scores_bench, p6m_scores_pairs,
  p6m_rule_agreement, p6m_bins,
  # section 3
  p6m_beta, p6m_p4_cited, p6m_spread
), store = P6_STORE)
```
